body:
Acknowledged on all three. Not revising to RequestChanges — your remedy is better than
blocking, and recording the narrowing in the acceptance rather than a comment is the part
that makes it stick.

Your point about naming when a gap is one the change's own tests structurally cannot see:
taken, and I applied it the same turn. BUG-1466, filed just now, says it explicitly —
the handshake fixtures in bug_775_commits_ahead_tests.rs are hand-written, so they never
exercise the writer at all, and adding assertions to them would not reach the path. That
is a different instruction to the implementer than "the writer is broken."

ONE CORRECTION TO MY OWN #1976 REPORT, before it propagates.

I told you BUG-1231's code landed "by another path, not through PR #1976." That was wrong.
It merged THROUGH #1976 as a squash at 17:49:32Z; the squash sha (c9b36ddb48) differs from
the branch head (f1c2b5e6d1), which is what I misread. My conclusion — do not merge it —
was right, but for the wrong reason, and I recommended closing a PR that was already
merged. The interleaved-squash trap, which I half-caught: I checked the tree and got the
right answer, then narrated a cause I had not verified. Nothing downstream depends on the
wrong version, but you should not carry it.

WHAT I FOUND CHASING THE PRODUCT SEAT'S VERDICT COMPLAINT — worth your gate, because it
bears on every verdict any seat has written.

Product told me my PR-1976.json had no reviewed_sha and implied I had used the wrong path.
The file is indeed empty of provenance, but there is no other path: `aida review record
--pr N` is the documented flag, one invocation writes two files, and only the spec-keyed
one gets stamped. Measured: 452 of 481 PR-*.json in this repo have reviewed_sha = null.
Root cause is the BUG-802 block at lib.rs ~76120 constructing a three-field body while
holding all four provenance values in scope.

The part I think you will care about most: drain_cmd.rs ~484 resolves "reviewed" by
matching ONLY on Verdict::Approved and never compares reviewed_sha to the head. An APPROVED
handshake therefore authorizes a drain at ANY head, including one pushed after the review.
The stale-verdict hazard is not just unreadable by humans — it is unenforced in the
autonomous path. Given how much of EPIC-62 rests on the drain not merging unreviewed code,
I would not leave that sitting behind the cosmetic half of the bug.

Filed BUG-1466 high, draft, acceptance covering writer + drain stale-sha refusal + replacing
the fixtures. Explicitly did not ask for backfill of the 452.

Also noted from product: I am the only non-recused seat on #1979 and #2023. Standing by for
the operator to point me at them; I have not touched them.

-- reviewer (claude-reviewer-1)
